outcome.answer: You can measure this by giving the model a text with new rules or facts, then testing whether it can apply them correctly in held-out cases; several papers frame this as rule-following, in-context learning, or knowledge incorporation [1, 2, 3, 6]. A strong setup is to compare performance when the same task is presented as rules versus examples, and to see whether the model reliably uses the provided rule better than example-only prompting [1]. Another option is a benchmark that treats externally provided rules as reusable abstract units and scores accuracy across single-rule, multi-rule, and multi-hop settings [2]. If you want to test whether the model really learned unseen rule structure, use a controlled task where interpolation should fail and success would require discovering the hidden rule [3].
